chapter_title_en: Better to Kill a Thousand Innocents
chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 428: The Purge Begins — “Better to Kill a Thousand Innocents”
chapter_meta_description: The capital is sealed. A brutal bounty is placed on every Zuowandao head. As the city descends into a bloodbath, Li Huowang is forced to watch, unable to stop the slaughter or save his own humanity.
og_title: The Capital’s Hunt Begins: “Better to Kill a Thousand Innocents”
og_description: The Supervisory Heavenly Office unleashes a reign of terror on the capital. Li Huowang witnesses the horrific cost of the order: “Better to kill a thousand innocents than let one Zuowandao escape.”
twitter_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian 428: The City Burns
twitter_description: The capital is a sealed hunting ground. Li Huowang can only watch as the purge turns innocent lives into collateral damage. A brutal, moral gut-punch of a chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: A secret society whose name means "The Way of Sitting in Forgetfulness," a perversion of a Daoist meditative concept; they are liars and tricksters dedicated to spreading confusion and chaos.
Longevity elixirs used as currency by the Supervisory Heavenly Office; consuming them extends one’s lifespan, but impure versions can lead to monstrous transformations.
The highest-ranked inner circles of the Zuowandao; killing one of these leaders brings massive rewards.
The supreme leader of the Supervisory Heavenly Office, a figure of immense bureaucratic and supernatural power.
Protective deities or warrior images pasted on Chinese doors during Lunar New Year; in the Dao-Twisted World, their impotence at protecting a family deepens the sense of horror.
In the Dao-Twisted World, a grotesque, malformed creature created from a person who lives past 120 without achieving immortality and forcibly extends life with elixirs.
A Buddhist concept of hell divided into eighteen levels, each with unique punishments; Li Huowang compares the capital’s state to this underworld.
A large, distinctive blade often associated with executioners or bandits in Chinese martial fiction.
The Buddha of Infinite Light in Pure Land Buddhism; the monk's chant is a desperate attempt to guide the dead in a world where even prayer seems futile.
